parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.label: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 — 25 European languages (default)
pros: Best accuracy for European languages, incl. German and English
Fastest option — transcribes far faster than real time on the CPU
Detects the language by itself, with punctuation and capitalization
cons: Only 25 (European) languages — no Chinese, Japanese or Korean
Less robust than Whisper on heavy accents or noisy recordings

whisper-small.label: Whisper Small — 90+ languages
pros: Widest coverage — 90+ languages incl. Chinese, Japanese, Korean
Robust with accents, background noise and far-from-mic speech
Accepts a spoken-language hint (setting below)
cons: Several times slower than Parakeet
Can invent text during long silences or music

whisper-base.label: Whisper Base — smallest, less accurate
pros: Smallest download and lowest memory use
Fastest of the Whisper family
Same 90+ language coverage
cons: Least accurate — noticeably more transcription errors
Struggles with accents, jargon and people talking over each other

qwen3-asr-0.6b.label: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B — 30 languages incl. Chinese, Japanese, Korean
pros: Wide coverage — 30 languages plus 22 Chinese dialects
Published accuracy on par with Whisper Large v3, well ahead of Whisper Small
Detects the language by itself; accepts a spoken-language hint
cons: Larger download than Parakeet and Whisper
About half as fast as Parakeet on the CPU

cohere-transcribe.label: Cohere Transcribe 2B — 14 languages, most accurate
pros: Most accurate open model for English and the major European languages
14 languages incl. German, English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean
cons: Needs the spoken language set — it can't detect it
Largest download and memory use (≈3 GB on disk, ≈5 GB RAM)
About half as fast as Parakeet on the CPU

nemotron-3-diarization.label: Nemotron 3 Diarization — up to 8 speakers (default)
pros: Fewer mixed-up or invented speakers
More than twice as fast as the classic model
Follows people talking over each other
cons: Tells at most 8 speakers apart
No tuning settings

pyannote-3.0.label: Classic (pyannote 3.0) — any number of speakers
pros: No limit on the number of speakers
Tunable: speaker separation and minimum speaking time
cons: Mixes up or invents speakers more often
Less than half as fast

qwen3.5-0.8b.label: Qwen 3.5 0.8B — tiny, fastest
pros: Notes in seconds, even on modest hardware
Tiny download, runs in about 1 GB of memory
cons: Short, plain notes that miss nuance
Action items often incomplete; weakest outside English

qwen3.5-2b.label: Qwen 3.5 2B — fast, light
pros: Quick summaries with about 2 GB of memory
Clearly better notes than the 0.8B
cons: Takeaways stay brief — subtle decisions can be missed
Less reliable than the 4B in languages other than English

qwen3.5-4b.label: Qwen 3.5 4B — balanced (default)
pros: Good balance of quality and speed
Reliable takeaways and action items
Solid notes in German, English and other major languages
cons: Needs roughly 3–4 GB of free memory
A long meeting takes a few minutes on CPU-only machines

qwen3.5-9b.label: Qwen 3.5 9B — strongest, slowest
pros: Highest-quality notes — best for long, complex or multilingual meetings
Most faithful decisions and action items
cons: Large download and needs roughly 7 GB of free memory
Slowest — can take many minutes without GPU acceleration
